subject: Pricing units and SLAs — case studies and negotiation scenarios
messages:
From: Jessica Lin <jessica.lin@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on minimums / rounding / session windows for enterprise pricing

Hi Monica —

Thanks again for the demo last week — the model latency and autoscaling looked great. Before we move to procurement there are a few specific billing mechanics our finance team wants clarified so legal can draft the SOW:

1) How are billing units counted for multi-request sessions that reuse context? Example: our product opens a user session that issues 6 calls (short prompts + a final summarization). Do you charge per call, per token aggregated across the session, or something else?

2) Are there minimum-charge windows or per-request floors? If so, how is rounding handled (per-request, per-minute, per-session)?

3) For streaming responses do you round up to the nearest billing unit as tokens are emitted, or is streaming charged on actual tokens consumed?

4) For Dedicated instances — do committed capacity discounts change rounding/minimum behavior? Our procurement team wants to understand if we can get rounding exceptions for the first billing period while we ramp.

Can you send a couple of short worked examples and an invoice-like sample so Finance can see the numbers? I attached a short summary doc with our expected call pattern.

Cheers,
Jessica
Senior Product Ops — Acme Analytics

Attachment: acme_call_pattern.csv (CSV, referenced in-body)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Lin <jessica.lin@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on minimums / rounding / session windows for enterprise pricing

Hi Jessica —

Thanks for the very clear list — I pulled together short, concrete examples below plus a recommended negotiation playbook we typically use for pilots and first-quarter ramps. Attaching our public Pricing FAQ as well.

Summary of how Redwood counts and rounds (short answers):
- Per-request measurement: Each API call is metered by tokens consumed (prompt + generated tokens) at the time the request completes.
- Minimum/rounding unit: Hosted API has a 50-token per-request floor and rounds up to the nearest 50-token increment for billing.
- Session aggregation: We do not automatically aggregate multiple discrete requests into a single billing unit unless they traverse the same "session-affinity" sticky routing and are explicitly flagged as the same conversation by the SDK; even then, the rounding floor still applies per RPC boundary.
- Streaming: Charged on actual emitted tokens, but we still apply the 50-token floor to the first chunk; subsequent streamed chunks are billed by actual tokens (no additional floor).
- Dedicated/Private: For Dedicated reservations, we can waive the per-request floor and bill on actual tokens consumed for the committed capacity portion of usage. Non-committed bursts still follow the hosted rounding behavior.

Worked example 1 — short session, hosted API
- Calls: 3 requests in one user session. Tokens: 40, 120, 360.
- Rounding/floor per request: 50, 120 (already above floor), 360.
- Billed tokens: 50 + 120 + 360 = 530 tokens.

Worked example 2 — streaming response
- Single request with streaming emission totaling 180 emitted tokens. First chunk produced 30 tokens, then 150 more over time.
- Billing: first chunk bumped to 50 (floor). Remaining 150 billed actual. Total billed tokens = 50 + 150 = 200 tokens.

Worked example 3 — Dedicated reserved capacity (50k committed tokens/mo)
- Same 3-call session as example 1 above, but calls served from committed pool. For the committed portion we bill exact tokens: 40 + 120 + 360 = 520 tokens (no per-request floor). If usage is below commit and we grant a ramp credit for month 1, we can further adjust the invoice per the term sheet.

Negotiation playbook (what sales/legal offer during initial procurement):
- Pilot ramp credit: offer a one-time credit equal to 20% of expected first-month spend or cap of $5k to cover rounding inefficiencies while integrations stabilize.
- Floor waiver for committed usage: if customer signs a Dedicated commit >= $50k/mo, waive per-request floor for the committed pool.
- Invoicing example: provide a sample invoice PDF that shows both billed tokens and gross-to-net adjustments (credits, waived floors).

Next steps: I attached a sample invoice layout and a short term-sheet language we usually propose. Ben — can you add the explicit SOW clause for the waiver + invoice line item? Karthik — can you confirm the Dedicated behavior and whether we need any engineering flag to treat calls as "session-affinity"?

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Monica.Patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Jessica Lin <jessica.lin@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on minimums / rounding / session windows for enterprise pricing

Jessica / Monica —

Quick note from a contracting perspective. Below is suggested SOW language that covers the floor waiver and invoicing transparency. Legal can refine but we'd like to capture the commercial intent exactly.

Suggested clause (SOW / Annex):
"Billing measurement: Redwood Inference measures usage in whole tokens consumed (prompt + generation). For Hosted API calls, Redwood applies a per-request minimum billing increment of fifty (50) tokens and rounds up to the nearest increment. For Dedicated committed pools (as defined in the Order Form), Redwood shall bill actual tokens consumed for usage drawn from the committed pool; host-level per-request minimums shall not apply to committed usage.

Floor waiver & ramp credit: Redwood agrees to apply a one-time ramp adjustment equal to twenty percent (20%) of Customer's estimated first month usage or a cap of five thousand dollars (USD $5,000), whichever is lower, against invoices issued for the first billing cycle following start of production traffic.

Invoice transparency: Redwood will include a line-itemized usage appendix with each invoice listing the number of calls, raw tokens by call, applied rounding/floor adjustments, and any credits or adjustments made under this SOW."

If that language looks OK we can add it as Annex A and wire it to the e-sign flow. Evelyn — please attach the sample invoice with line items and confirm the format is ready for the DocuSign package.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachment: negotiation-term-sheet-draft.docx

To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acmeanalytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on minimums / rounding / session windows for enterprise pricing

Thanks Monica and Ben — this is very helpful and addresses most of our questions. A couple follow-ups: 

- Can you produce the sample invoice (the attached example-invoice looks close) with the three sample sessions from your worked examples so our finance team can walk through the math line by line?
- For the ramp credit, would Redwood consider extending the cap to $7,500 if we commit to a 6-month pilot with biweekly check-ins? That would make the ramp economics painless for us.

If you're comfortable with Ben's SOW language, we can share with legal and route the DocuSign. Please put the sample invoice in the shared Drive link and flag it in the DocuSign bundle.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Jessica
Senior Product Ops — Acme Analytics
